sections.html:
Roseburg is both seat and largest city of Douglas County in southwest Oregon, a county of about 5,071 square miles that runs from the Pacific at sea level to 9,182 feet at Mount Thielsen. The federal government owns more than half the land, mostly through the Forest Service and the Bureau of Land Management. Towns include Sutherlin, Winchester, Myrtle Creek, Canyonville, Reedsport and Riddle, and the distances between them are long.

The 2020 Census counted 111,201 residents, with a median age of 48.1 and 26.8% of people aged 65 or older. About 59.6% lived in urban areas and 40.4% in rural ones. Forest products, mining, agriculture, fishing and recreation drive the economy, with forest products the largest of those.

An older population means many owners are long-term and many homes pass through estates. Heirs who live elsewhere can face a vacant house in a small town and tax bills still addressed to the deceased owner. A property may also carry a deferral lien or a farm or forest special assessment, covered below.

sections.h2: Weather and upkeep on rural lots
sections.html:
Roseburg sits at 475 feet and gets about 33.35 inches of precipitation a year. Winters are mild and wet, and summers are warm. Houses on forested or hillside lots have their own upkeep needs:

  • roofs and gutters that collect needles and leaves
  • decks, stairs and retaining walls on sloped ground
  • septic systems and wells on rural parcels
  • fire-season clearance around buildings near timber

If you sell a rural house, ask the county what permits and records exist for the septic system and any outbuildings.

sections.h2: Douglas County tax numbers and offices
sections.html:
For fiscal year 2024-25, about $135.4 million in tax was imposed on $12.23 billion of assessed value. The average rate was $11.07 per $1,000 of assessed value, and the Measure 5 rate was $6.98 per $1,000 of Measure 5 value. The average reflects the mix of taxing districts here, so your bill depends on your address.

OfficeLocation and phone
Tax Office1036 SE Douglas Ave, CH205, Roseburg; 541-440-4253
Assessor (Appraisal)1036 SE Douglas Ave, CH206, Roseburg; 541-440-4222

sections.h2: Due dates and how to pay
sections.html:
The bill splits into thirds that fall due November 15, then February 15, then May 15. Interest on late amounts is 1.333% per month, which adds up to 16% over a year. Weekend due dates roll forward a business day. Card payments made online have to be completed by 11:59 p.m. Pacific that day.

  • Account numbers carry a letter prefix, R, M, U or P, such as R12345.
  • A yellow statement shows that a mortgage company or the deferral program requested the tax information.
  • Online fees are 2.49% for credit cards, $3.95 for debit and $3.00 for e-checks, and one account can be paid per transaction.
  • Checks go to Douglas County, with no cash by mail and no post-dated checks.
  • Properties in tax foreclosure or bankruptcy cannot pay online.

When more than one year is owed, payments apply to the earliest year first. The Tax Office opens weekdays from 8 a.m. until 5 p.m. and shuts for lunch between noon and 1 p.m. The Assessor's hours are shorter, with Wednesday open only until noon and other days by appointment, so call 541-440-4222 before you drive in. The tax collector's mailing address is PO Box 8403, Medford, OR 97501.

Three years of delinquency opens the door to foreclosure on real property, and after judgment the owner gets two years to redeem. ORS chapter 312 lets recorded interest holders, their heirs and lien holders redeem. The price is the judgment amount, interest, a 5% penalty and a fee.

The foreclosure steps come in late summer after the third year: a list is prepared in July, published and sent to the district attorney by mid-August, and the district attorney seeks a judgment by September 16. For a specific account, call the Tax Office at 541-440-4253.

The Property Value Appeals Board takes petitions through December 31, shifting to the next business day when that is a weekend. Its hearings begin on or after the first Monday in February and end by March 15.

Start with the Assessor at 541-440-4222. The office estimates market value for each property and manages farm, forest and exemption programs, so it can explain how your value was set before you file.

Forest and farm land can carry a lower special assessment, and leaving the program can cost money. Disqualification triggers a recovery penalty reaching back up to five years for most land and up to ten for EFU, MPA and STF land. Ask the Assessor before you split or change the use of a parcel.

Seniors may be in the state deferral program, which places a lien at 6% interest. Selling the house ends the deferral. The unpaid balance must then be paid by August 15 of the following year, and heirs can be liable if the owner has died.

Oregon's seller disclosure form (ORS 105.464) travels with a written offer. After receiving it the buyer has five days to revoke. A personal representative or a financial institution that foreclosed may complete only part of the form.

sections.h2: Questions to ask before a rural sale
sections.html:
Long distances between towns mean a buyer may drive a long way to see your house, so the details need to be ready. Know the water source, the septic status and how the road is maintained. Say whether any part of the land is in a farm or forest program.

If the house sits near timber, ask what fire-season clearance applies. If it came from an estate, find out whether the tax bills have been going to the right name, and have the Tax Office update the mailing address. Heirs often learn about a late balance only when the notice arrives at an old address.

sections.h2: Selling a Douglas County house with taxes owed
sections.html:
Back taxes can come out of the sale proceeds at the title company, so you need not scrape together cash beforehand. Ask the Tax Office for a payoff matching your closing date, and expect the oldest year to be paid first.

Rural houses, inherited houses and houses with a deferral lien all need a few extra documents. Gather the deed or probate paperwork, any septic or well records, and the latest statement. A cash buyer takes the house in its current condition, so roof, deck and clearance work does not have to happen before you sell.

faqs.q: When are Douglas County property taxes due?
faqs.a: They are due November 15, February 15 and May 15. When the 15th falls on a weekend, the due date moves to the first business day of the next week.

faqs.q: What is the interest rate on late Douglas County property taxes?
faqs.a: Late interest is 1.333% a month, which is 16% a year. Payments apply to the earliest tax year first when more than one year is owed.

faqs.q: Where is the Douglas County Tax Office?
faqs.a: The Tax Office is at 1036 SE Douglas Ave, room CH205, in Roseburg, and the phone is 541-440-4253. It is open Monday to Friday, 8 a.m. to 5 p.m., and closes from noon to 1 p.m.

faqs.q: Can I pay a Douglas County tax bill online?
faqs.a: Yes, by searching your property on the county site and choosing Pay My Bills. Fees apply, and properties in tax foreclosure or bankruptcy cannot be paid online.

faqs.q: What happens to a tax deferral lien if I sell my Douglas County home?
faqs.a: The deferred taxes, 6% interest and recording costs come due after a sale. Payment is due by August 15 of the next year.
